sources_quoted.claim: Unified Memory is not fully supported on WSL 2
sources_quoted.quote: Unified Memory - Full Managed Memory Support is not available on Windows native and therefore WSL 2 will not support it for the foreseeable future.
sources_quoted.section: 5.1. Known Limitations for Linux CUDA Applications

sources_quoted.claim: Managed-memory applications on WSL2 see reduced performance and high system memory usage
sources_quoted.quote: If your application is using Managed Memory, your application could see reduced performance and high system memory usage.
sources_quoted.section: 5.1. Known Limitations for Linux CUDA Applications

sources_quoted.claim: Concurrent CPU/GPU access to managed memory is unsupported on WSL2
sources_quoted.quote: Concurrent CPU/GPU access is not supported. CUDA queries will say whether it is supported or not and applications are expected to check this.
sources_quoted.section: 5.1. Known Limitations for Linux CUDA Applications

sources_quoted.claim: Pinned system memory is limited on WSL2
sources_quoted.quote: Pinned system memory (example: System memory that an application makes resident for GPU accesses) availability for applications is limited.
sources_quoted.section: 5.1. Known Limitations for Linux CUDA Applications

sources_quoted.claim: WSL falls under the limited unified-memory paradigm
sources_quoted.quote: On Windows, including Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), and on some Tegra systems, a limited subset of unified memory functionality is available. On these systems, managed memory is available, but migration between CPU and GPUs behaves differently.

sources_quoted.claim: GPU memory oversubscription is forbidden under the limited paradigm (decisive quote)
sources_quoted.quote: Oversubscription of GPU memory is not allowed

sources_quoted.claim: Oversubscription IS allowed only under full unified-memory support (the Linux/HMM case, not WSL)
sources_quoted.quote: Oversubscription is allowed: an application may allocate more managed memory than is physically available on the GPU

sources_quoted.claim: No GPU-side page faulting / on-demand migration on Windows and WSL
sources_quoted.quote: Data Migration and Coherency: Fine-grained movement of the managed data to GPU on-demand is not supported. Whenever a GPU kernel is launched all managed memory generally has to be transferred to GPU memory to avoid faulting on memory access. Page faulting is only supported from the CPU side.
sources_quoted.section: 4.1.3. Unified Memory on Windows, WSL, and Tegra

sources_quoted.claim: Managed allocations cannot exceed physical VRAM on these platforms
sources_quoted.quote: GPU Memory Oversubscription: They cannot allocate more managed memory than the physical size of GPU memory.
sources_quoted.section: 4.1.3. Unified Memory on Windows, WSL, and Tegra

sources_quoted.claim: GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY is documented as a Linux mechanism
sources_quoted.quote: The environment variable `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1` can be used to enable unified memory in Linux. This allows swapping to system RAM instead of crashing when the GPU VRAM is exhausted. In Windows this setting is available in the NVIDIA control panel as `System Memory Fallback`.
